Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: On August 24, Irene passed over the British Overseas Territory of Turks and Caicos Islands at Category 1 strength. The hurricane produced high winds that blew off roofs and downed power lines throughout the territory. In Cockburn Town, residences reported loss of power, and light poles were toppled. Many homes on Grand Turk Island also reported a loss of electricity during Irene's passage, although structural damage in the area was limited. The strongest of the rains and gusts occurred in Providenciales, where light wind damage was reported to roofs and resorts. The Grand Turk cruise port also sustained some minor damage from the storm, but operations resumed three days after impact.
The extreme winds damaged at least 40 homes on Mayaguana Island.
Dozens of homes on Acklins were completely obliterated. On the latter island, the hurricane reportedly wiped out 90 percent of the Lovely Bay settlement.
Similar winds tore off the roof and shattered the windows out of a high school on Crooked Island, where wind gusts as high as 99 mph (159 km/h) were reported.
A local church on Crooked Island partially collapsed due to the storm.
The worst of the destruction occurred in Cat Island, characterized by widespread shattered glass and torn houses.

In North Jersey, two people drowned in their cars in Bergen County.[12]
Two people also drowned in Passaic County.[2]

In Pequannock, flooding damaged around 250 houses, causing an estimated $5.5 million in damage.

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: Ninety people died during the mass evacuation in Texas, accounting for more fatalities than the direct impacts of Hurricane Rita and constituting a majority of the fatalities associated with the storm.[h]

Another 10 people died during the evacuations of chronic health facilities.[14]

At around 6:00 a.m. on September 23, a motorcoach evacuating 44 residents and staff from a nursing home in Bellaire, Texas, caught fire on Interstate 45 near Wilmer, Texas, en route for Dallas, killing 23 people.[17]
An investigation conducted by The Houston Chronicle found another 18 deaths of nursing home residents associated with the evacuation.[39]
During the motorcoach incident on September 23, besides the 23 fatalities, the vehicle fire resulted in 2 serious injuries and 19 minor injuries among the survivors.

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: Even though it passed well south of Barbados on September 6, potent winds damaged 531 homes to varying degree.
In Grenada, at least 89% of the island—or 28,000 of 31,000 homes—experienced damage when Ivan passed directly over the island on September 7.
The capital, St. George's, was severely damaged and several notable buildings were destroyed, including the two largest hospitals in Grenada.
Lighter effects occurred in Trinidad and Tobago with most damage confined to Tobago, where at least 45 homes lost their roofs and twenty villages suffered various forms of damage.
Large waves and high storm surge battered the coastlines of Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, washing away 2 homes, destroying 19 and damaging 40.
As Ivan passed well south of Barbados on September 6, one person drowned due to flooding.
In Grenada, 41 people lost their lives during the hurricane.
In Trinidad and Tobago, specifically in Tobago, one person died from a fallen tree.
Monetary losses on Barbados surmounted $5 million as Ivan passed well south of the island on September 6.
Damage on Grenada totaled $830.7 million (equivalent to $1.38 billion in 2024) when Ivan passed directly over the island on September 7.
Damage in Trinidad and Tobago was estimated at $4.9 million, with most impacts on Tobago.
Losses for Saint Vincent and the Grenadines totaled $40 million amid severe coastal damage from high storm surge.
Southern portions of Saint Lucia incurred $2.6 million worth in damage to homes and crops due to strong winds and rough surf.
A developing spiral band caused flooding and resulted in $1.1 million worth in structural damage in Aruba on September 9.

Event_Names: Timeline of the 1991 Atlantic hurricane season
Time_Annotation: The season officially began on June 1, 1991, and ended on November 30. These dates, adopted by convention, historically describe the period in each year when most subtropical or tropical cyclogenesis occurs in the Atlantic Ocean.
Administrative_Areas_Annotation: Hurricane Bob, which brushed the Outer Banks of North Carolina and made landfall in Rhode Island while causing extensive damage in New England, underscores the impact on the United States. Additionally, the Perfect Storm developed off the coast of eastern Nova Scotia, indicating effects in Canada.
Main_Event_Annotation: The timeline documents tropical cyclone activities—such as the development of Tropical Storm Ana, the intensification of Hurricane Bob, and the extratropical transition of the Perfect Storm—characteristic of a Tropical Storm/Cyclone event.
Hazards_Annotation: Based on the association table for a Tropical Storm/Cyclone, the hazards include wind (evident from high sustained wind reports and structural damages), flood (from heavy rains and coastal inundation), and lightning, which are typical for such events.

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: At 01:45 UTC on July 7, a large tornado touched down at the Atlanta Motor Speedway in Hampton in Henry County, causing heavy damage to the speedway facilities, destroying a gas station and shattering windows of a nine‐story condominium.
The first event was an F0 twister in Mobile County, which was on the ground for about three minutes, during which a few homes and outbuildings sustained roof damage.
An F1 tornado touched down north of Autaugaville, which damaged an outbuilding and knocked down several trees, with damage estimated at $14,000.
Another F1 tornado hit northwest of Tuskegee, which destroyed an automobile repair shop (and injured a man), with damage estimated at $48,000.
There was an F0 twister in Montgomery County that remained on the ground for eight minutes, severely damaging a baseball complex and blowing down trees; the tornado's cost was estimated at $22,000.
There was also an F0 tornado that took a 5.6 mi path between Macon and Elmore counties, during which it damaged a few roofs.
An F0 tornado hit southeast of Fayetteville, knocking down hundreds of trees and causing $1.95 million in damage to buildings and businesses.

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Num: damaged a church and several homes
Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: A tornado touched down near I-75 West McDonough, damaging a church and several homes, with damage estimated at $150,000.
There was an F0 tornado in Meriwether County, which damaged two buildings and a vehicle.

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Num: damaged a mobile home and a barn
Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: A tornado near Spartanburg touched down just south of the NC/SC border; after crossing into North Carolina, it lifted a mobile home and damaged a barn.

Locations: near North Carolina Highway 16 south of Taylorsville
Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Num: destroyed a mobile home and severely damaged the roofs of three buildings
Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: A F2 tornado touched down near North Carolina Highway 16 south of Taylorsville, destroying a mobile home and severely damaging the roofs of three buildings, with damage estimated at $150,000.

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Num: destroyed a dairy farm and damaged buildings
Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: Another F2 tornado took an 8.6 mi path through Iredell and Yadkin counties, causing $2.4 million in damage, including a destroyed dairy farm and damaged buildings.

Near Hazel Green, Alabama, a high-end EF0 tornado damaged several businesses, snapped tree branches, and ripped the roof off a mobile home. One person was injured, the only injury of the outbreak.[20]
Two weak tornadoes also touched down in North Carolina during the morning hours of January 3 before the outbreak ended, one of which caused EF1 damage to some hog barns near Newton Grove.

The most significant damage was inflicted to farmsteads and homes outside of town, where a house had its roof torn off, another house had its attached garage destroyed, and multiple other homes suffered extensive roof and window damage. Barns, farm buildings, garages, metal grain silos, and sheds were completely destroyed as well, with debris scattered long distances across fields. Farm animals were killed, RV campers and several semi-trailers were rolled, while farming equipment and irrigation pivots were damaged.
Another storm produced a brief EF1 tornado that snapped trees and collapsed a barn in Addison, Vermont.
Another storm produced a brief EF1 tornado that snapped trees and destroyed some outbuildings near Chesterfield, New Hampshire.

An EF3 tornado near Cason, Texas, killed one person, injured eight others, completely destroyed multiple homes and mobile homes, knocked over metal truss transmission towers, and caused major tree damage.

Later that night, a brief but strong EF2 tornado touched down near Sardis, tearing roofs off of a few homes and causing significant tree damage.
An EF0 tornado caused minor damage to trees, power lines, and a barn near Big Rock.

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: The first tornado of the day was rated high-end F1 and hit the village of Casekow in eastern Germany, snapping trees, destroying horse stables, and causing substantial roof damage to several residences in town. Some large farmhouses sustained considerable damage outside of Casekow as well.
An F1 tornado damaged trees, roofs, and outbuildings in Skwierzyna. Pieces of wood were speared into the exterior wall of one structure in the village as well.

An F2 tornado passed near Sucharzewo, causing significant damage to brick homes and outbuildings, including a brick cow shed that collapsed, killing a bull. Swaths of trees were mowed down in rural areas near Sucharzewo, and some debarking occurred.
In Krzykosy, an unrated tornado downed trees and power lines, and damaged the roofs of several residences, including one that was completely unroofed.

An F2 tornado struck Młodzikowice and another impacted Grzywna Szlachecka, largely destroying several masonry outbuildings, snapping many trees, damaging vehicles, and causing roof and window damage to homes in and around both villages.

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Num: A church, some homes, and a duck farm
Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: A church and some homes in the Stara Ciświca area had roofing torn off as a result of an F2 tornado, and major tree and outbuilding damage occurred as well. A duck farm near the village was significantly damaged, and several ducks were killed at that location.
An F1 tornado tore the sheet metal roof off a house near Żurawin.
Four other F1 tornadoes also caused considerable tree and structural damage in and around the small villages and towns of Łaski, Łęka, Lipicze Górne, and Aleksandria.

To the northeast of Kalisz, an F2 tornado inflicted severe roof damage to homes, destroyed outbuildings, damaged a soccer field, and scattered debris across fields and passed through or near multiple villages.

Another strong F2 tornado struck Dobrzyca, where multiple homes had their roofs and second-floor exterior walls ripped off, and streets were littered with debris. Power lines were downed, and large trees were snapped in a wooded area as well.

Yet another F2 tornado caused heavy damage to buildings in Lgów, scattering debris throughout the small community. Homes had their roofs torn off, outbuildings were destroyed, debris was strewn across fields, cars were damaged, and numerous trees were snapped in a forest.
A strong F2 tornado ripped the roofs off of homes, destroyed large brick outbuildings, damaged a greenhouse, and injured two people as it impacted Wójcice and Smaszków.
Another F2 tornado flipped a car and destroyed a summer home near Słomków Kościelny.

In the city of Kraków, a short-lived tornado of unknown intensity caused a construction crane to collapse, resulting in two deaths and two injuries. A few buildings in Kraków had roofing blown off, and cars were damaged by flying debris.

Another damaging but unrated tornado struck Sierosław, where every building in town sustained some degree of damage, a few of which had their roofs torn off and sustained some damage to their brick exterior walls. Farms sustained severe damage outside of town, metal truss transmission towers were blown over, and two semi-trucks were overturned, injuring one of the drivers.
A brief tornado also produced F2 damage along the shore of Lake Powidzkie near Kosewo, snapping large trees, tossing boats, and damaging a residential building.

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Num: 2 medical clinic buildings partially unroofed; 1 supermarket with roof damage; 1 brick farm home with roofing removed; 1 large brick farm building partially destroyed; 1 smaller outbuilding completely destroyed; 1 large masonry-construction church with steeple torn off; additional roof damage to many homes, businesses, and a school
Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: The first F2 wedge tornado in Germany touched down west of Lippstadt causing damage in the villages of Eickelborn and Benninghausen (two medical clinic buildings partially unroofed and a supermarket sustaining roof damage), then in a rural area (a brick farm home had its roofing removed, a large brick farm building was partially destroyed, a smaller outbuilding was completely destroyed, and a masonry-construction church had its steeple torn off) before causing roof damage to many homes, businesses, and a school in Lippstadt.[153]

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Num: Homes, churches, schools, businesses, and apartment buildings sustained partial to total roof loss; 1 apartment building unroofed with partial failure; 1 office building, 1 large furniture store, a used car business, and warehouses heavily damaged
Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: The second F2 tornado in Paderborn caused major damage with various structures (homes, churches, schools, businesses, and apartment buildings) suffering roof loss, including an unroofed apartment building with partial failure of exterior walls, and significant damage to an office building, a large furniture store, a used car business, and warehouses.[154]

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Num: Dozens of trees and roofs damaged; many homes sustained heavy roof damage; a soccer field damaged; a large industrial building had its roof blown off; outbuildings damaged or destroyed
Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: The third tornado, a high-end F1, struck the towns of Ovenhausen and Lütmarsen, where it damaged dozens of trees and roofs, many homes sustained heavy roof damage, a soccer field was damaged, a large industrial building had its roof blown off, and outbuildings were damaged or destroyed.[155]

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Num: A large house and a masonry building had roof structures completely destroyed; a small summer home destroyed; multiple other homes and buildings suffered major roof damage
Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: The fourth F2 tornado near Merxhausen, after flattening trees in a densely-forested area, struck Merxhausen causing a large house and a masonry building to lose their roof structures completely, a small summer home to be destroyed, and other homes and buildings to sustain major roof damage.[156]

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Num: Roof damage to homes; a frail brick-built garage partly collapsed
Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: The fifth tornado, rated low-end F1, hit Langelsheim along a 0.8 km path, causing roof damage to homes and partially collapsing a frail brick-built garage.[157]
A brief low-end F1 tornado in a suburban area in southwestern Herford caused roof and tree damage along its 0.65 km path.[158]
A rain-wrapped F1 tornado in Hillscheid downed additional trees and caused slight roof damage.

The most significant event of the outbreak was a very long-tracked EF3/F3/T6/IF3 tornado, which caused severe damage in multiple towns, with the most intense impact in Bihucourt where homes and other buildings sustained total loss of roofs and exterior walls.
The tornado eventually crossed into Belgium, causing tree and roof damage in a few villages before dissipating.
A few F1 tornadoes also caused considerable damage in the towns of Ferrières-en-Bray, Gaudechart, and Beaudéduit.

Significant damage to homes, an apartment building, the University of Wisconsin–Platteville campus, a gas station, power lines, and many trees occurred throughout Platteville.
Strong tornadoes continued touching down into the early morning hours of June 17, as an EF2 ripped roofs off of homes in residential areas of Madison, Wisconsin.

On June 18, additional intense tornadoes occurred across parts of South Dakota, including a highly photogenic EF4 tornado that swept away a farmhouse and debarked trees as it passed near Alpena.

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: A large, rain‐wrapped, EF3 wedge tornado struck Columbia, Mississippi, at around 2:30pm. As it entered town and crossed Marion School Rd, two brick homes were destroyed. Later, as it crossed Mississippi Highway 13, it heavily damaged several businesses and destroyed homes—with a brick house reduced to rubble and a small wood-frame home swept away—and further destroyed numerous metal-frame warehouse structures and storage units. On the east side, a National Guard armory sustained low‐end EF3 damage, several mobile homes were destroyed, and an outbuilding was lost.

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: Another tornado passed to the northwest of Laurel, Mississippi, causing mainly minor tree and roof damage, though a small area of EF2 damage was noted as one small, unanchored wood-frame home was swept away and a nearby mobile home was completely destroyed.
Three other weak tornadoes occurred the following day before the outbreak came to an end, including an EF1 that damaged 7 homes near Bristol, Georgia.

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: producing widespread, devastating damage as it impacted the southern part of Beauregard. A massive swath of large trees in this area was completely mowed down and debarked, and numerous manufactured homes were thrown and obliterated, with debris scattered in all directions and the metal frames of several of these homes being twisted around trees or never recovered. The most intense damage was inflicted to a well-built, anchor-bolted brick home that was leveled with a portion of the slab foundation swept clean of debris. Several block-foundation frame homes were leveled or swept completely away in this area, and windrowing of debris was noted.

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Num: multiple small and poorly constructed frame homes lost their roofs and exterior walls; bar and music venue sustained major structural damage; gas station sustained moderate damage
Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: Crossing County Road 179, the tornado entered the town of Smiths Station at high-end EF2 strength. In Smiths Station, multiple small and poorly constructed frame homes lost their roofs and exterior walls, a bar and music venue sustained major structural damage, a gas station sustained moderate damage, and numerous trees were downed. A cell tower was toppled, and a billboard sign was damaged.

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Num: Numerous manufactured homes obliterated; multiple other manufactured homes badly damaged; several frame homes severely damaged (one shifted 10 ft off its foundation, another had its second floor removed); an unanchored brick duplex swept from its foundation and leveled; one manufactured home rolled and destroyed
Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: Regaining low-end EF3 strength, the tornado proceeded to strike the north side of Talbotton, causing major damage in town. Numerous manufactured homes were obliterated with debris scattered up to a quarter mile away, multiple other manufactured homes were badly damaged, several frame homes sustained severe damage (including one shifted 10 ft off its foundation and another with its second floor removed), an unanchored brick duplex was swept from its foundation and leveled, and a manufactured home was rolled and destroyed.

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: The first tornadoes of the day occurred in the Midwest, where an EF1 tornado that touched down in Greenwood, Indiana, where several homes sustained damage.
Another tornado caused damage to homes in the Indianapolis suburb of Noblesville.
In Illinois, a tornado destroyed multiple outbuildings and downed trees near the town of Sciota.

The outbreak also spawned the only known tornado to touch down in Michigan during the month of December, an EF1 tornado that struck the Detroit suburb of Canton, causing considerable damage to vehicles, an industrial park, and a gas station.

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Num: completely destroying mobile homes, tearing roofs off of frame homes, and damaging cabins
Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: A strong EF2 tornado occurred near Marianna, Arkansas, completely destroying mobile homes, tearing roofs off of frame homes, and damaging cabins in the area.
A large EF3 tornado eventually touched down south of Clarksdale, Mississippi, killing two people and severely damaging or destroying about 15 homes in that area.
The tornado continued to the northeast, later snapping trees and destroying homes near Marks and Como before dissipating.

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Num: destroying multiple homes and a church, and completely leveling the town's post office
Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: Another destructive EF3 tornado struck the small community of Lutts, Tennessee after dark, destroying multiple homes and a church, and completely leveling the town's post office.
Additional scattered tornado activity occurred on the 24th and 25th, including a high-end EF2 tornado that caused heavy damage in the southwestern part of Birmingham, Alabama on Christmas Day.

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: A large EF3 tornado eventually touched down south of Clarksdale, Mississippi, killing two people and severely damaging or destroying about 15 homes in that area.

The same parent supercell produced another tornado further east of Como, a violent EF4 tornado that devastated 6 counties in Mississippi and Tennessee along a 75.09 miles (120.85 km) mile long path, killing 9 people.

Significant tornado activity continued through parts of Mississippi and Tennessee overnight, including an EF2 tornado that killed an elderly couple in their small, unanchored home near Linden, Tennessee.

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: The tornado touched down northwest of Bogata in Red River County, Texas, producing EF1 damage as it tore tin metal roofing off a large chicken house.

Moving to the northeast, the tornado reached mid-range EF3 strength as it crossed FM 411 to the east of the small community of Fulbright. A house collapsed and was pushed off its foundation, a nearby home was left with only interior walls standing, and a metal outbuilding was obliterated.
EF2 damage continued northwest of Clarksville, where multiple homes and outbuildings were damaged or destroyed along that segment of the path.
To the north of Clarksville, a house along SH 37 had much of its roof blown off, with trees snapped, and damage rated high-end EF1.
Just beyond the previous point, the tornado abruptly intensified along County Road 3105, and a large one‐story home was swept clean from its foundation.
In Acworth, the tornado (rated high-end EF3) destroyed multiple structures – notably, The Mount Olive Church and a house were completely leveled.
A double‐wide manufactured home in Acworth was lifted off the ground and tossed 50 yards (46 m).

Upon entering Oklahoma, mid-range EF2 damage was inflicted on several single‐family homes as the tornado moved through rural areas toward Idabel; some homes sustained roof and exterior wall loss while outbuildings were destroyed.

As the tornado re‐intensified upon entering Idabel, major structural damage occurred in southeastern Idabel: homes had roofs torn off, some exterior walls collapsed (including one home along Leesa Drive), and a two‐story home lost much of its second floor, with additional businesses damaged.
At the Idabel Country Club, numerous trees were snapped and, in one grove, debarked, while multiple homes were damaged by tornadic winds and falling trees.
The nearby Kiamichi Family Medical Center in Idabel suffered severe structural damage with roof and exterior wall loss, metal beams twisted and façade torn off.
Continuing through eastern Idabel, the tornado crossed Southeast Lincoln Road and completely leveled the Donut Crossing donut shop and a nearby tire shop.
After crossing East Washington Street (SH-3), the tornado produced EF3 damage by completely flattening the Trinity Baptist Church and destroying a nearby doctor's office and local bank.
In the northeastern fringes of Idabel, as the tornado exited the town, there was mainly EF1 damage with a narrower EF2 swath where a house at Meadow Lane had a large portion of its roof ripped off.
Past Idabel, the tornado maintained strength through unpopulated wooded areas, downing numerous trees and destroying some chicken houses.
Between Broken Bow and Eagletown, at the intersection of Craig Road and Red Arrow Road, a double-wide mobile home was destroyed and an elevator structure was blown off the top of a large silo.

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: As the tornado entered the west side of Helena, it caused minor roof damage to homes and downed trees. Mainly shingle, siding, and fence damage was noted in this area, though a house that was under construction collapsed. Later, as it moved through the north side of Helena, a few homes along Cunningham Lane sustained partial roof loss, and one home in town sustained destruction of its front porch overhang.

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Num: One home lost its roof and most exterior walls; another home was pushed off its foundation and leveled; multiple other homes suffered varying degrees of roof and exterior wall loss
Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: The tornado reached its peak intensity as it struck the Eagle Point neighborhood just east of Meadowbrook. One home in the area lost its roof and most exterior walls, while another poorly-anchored home was pushed off its foundation and leveled (damage rated low-end EF3). Multiple other homes in the neighborhood suffered up to high-end EF2 damage.
The tornado weakened to EF1 strength as it moved over Double Oak Mountain and struck Vandiver, uprooting trees and damaging several homes on the northeast side of town.

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Num: destroying more mobile homes; one residence with roof torn off; two more shifted off foundations; several others with roofs ripped off; several barns and outbuildings destroyed
Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: Before reaching EF2 intensity for a third time east of the highway along Wellington Road, the tornado destroyed more mobile homes and snapped more trees. One residence had its roof torn off and exterior walls collapsed, two more were shifted off their foundations, and several others had their roofs ripped off. Several barns and outbuildings were also destroyed, and a few vehicles were flipped in this area.
To the northeast along Old Piedmont Gadsden Highway, another outbuilding was completely overturned. The tornado then crossed US 278 northwest of Piedmont, causing additional building damage.

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Num: Numerous homes damaged, with one home left with only its back wall standing

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Num: Damage to 1 metal building and another metal building; additional homes affected

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Num: 1 two‐story brick apartment building severely damaged; multiple buildings at Newnan High School damaged

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: A second tornado spawned by the same storm, rated as an EF1, touched down near Lake Amon G. Carter, damaging four homes and destroying one.
At 7:13 p.m. CDT, storm spotters reported a large tornado on the ground near Millsap in Parker County, which caused roof damage to several homes in the town.

An EF4 tornado hit the town of Granbury, Texas in Hood County around 8 p.m. CDT, damaging or destroying around 100 homes and killing six people, with the most severe damage occurring in the Rancho Brazos neighborhood.

The supercell that produced the Granbury tornado later spawned a very large EF3 tornado that hit the Fort Worth suburb of Cleburne in Johnson County around 9:30 p.m. CDT, producing its most significant damage just east of Lake Pat Cleburne.
The last twister of the outbreak touched down at 12:19 a.m., producing EF1 damage in the Ellis County town of Ennis, Texas, south-southeast of Dallas.
Two short-lived tornadoes touched down in Limestone County, Alabama on May 17, causing scattered damage to trees, roofs and a barn.
